## 2e5d92febde0

**Reproduced defect — one seed per distinct color is an unrefuted shortcut.**

Current generator SHA-256: `74363ebf81e32799aeb6376de6818c49b8bb266865eff0fc3efc8cb3946ac3cd`. Current canonical rule hash: `c0ffd80801b3`; the supported Racket `apply` receipt confirms the catalog hash matches.

The generator always calls `draw_distinct_colors(..., n=n)`, so it never emits two seeds of the same color. All four canonical pairs also use one unique color per seed. In a fresh 60-draw probe (seed 1729, sample indices 0–19 in each of easy/default/hard), all 60 inputs had equal seed count and distinct-color count. Therefore the plausible rival “extend only the first seed of each color” fits every canonical and sampled generated case.

The hand-made grid below is accepted by the current `self_check()` and belongs to the documented domain (two seeds in distinct columns, above the bottom row, zero background), but refutes that rival:

```text
02020
00000
00000
00000
00000
```

Racket extends both color-2 columns to the bottom; the rival extends only the first. Evidence: `checks/audit/2e5d92febde0/input.json`, `racket.json`, and `probe.json`. The Racket output was obtained with the supported `arcpuzzles apply` command recorded in the receipt. This independently confirms, rather than merely repeats, the prior unverified audit lead in `evidence/review_index.json`.

No files for this audit target were changed. Recommended repair: make repeated colors an ordinary observable axis value, implement `n_distinct_colors` truthfully, and add a lesson rival/witness that forces at least one repeated-color demonstration whenever the query contains repeated colors.

## 2e5d92febde0

Strong shortcut: **extend only one seed per distinct color**. It fits all four canonical demonstrations because every canonical seed color is unique, and it fits the current generator because `draw_distinct_colors(..., n=n)` guarantees one color per seed.

Exact counterexample, accepted by the current `self_check()` but never emitted by ordinary generation:

```text
02020
00000
00000
00000
00000
```

The intended rule extends both color-2 seeds to the bottom, yielding color-2 rays in columns 1 and 3. A “one ray per color” solver can extend only the left seed and still fit every current demonstration/generated case. Twenty-five sampled generated inputs all had unique seed colors, matching the construction. Recommended repair: allow repeated colors across distinct columns, expose `n_distinct_colors` truthfully instead of drawing `n` distinct colors unconditionally, and add a semantic witness comparing all-seeds versus one-per-color behavior. Probe details are in `checks/audit-probes.json`.
